summary: Configures and encodes an output packet's format fields (encoding type byte, bit depth byte, per-pixel stride byte, and total DWORD size) from session/state flag bits at this+0x60 and this+0x61, copying camera rotation DWORD at this+0x130 into the packet when the video flag is set.

local_names.a1: state object: flag bytes at 0x60/0x61 plus configuration at 0x10A, 0x130, 0x174
local_names.a2: output packet header buffer whose fields are rewritten and sized

operations.description: Reads flags byte at this+0x61; bit 0x10 enables the packet-format block that rewrites the encoding type byte and bit depth byte of the output packet.
When the encoding byte at a2+25 equals 3, rewrites it as 4 * (WORD at this+0x10A is non-zero ? 1 : 0) + 2, collapsing the type to 2 or 6 depending on that WORD.
Otherwise, when WORD at this+0x10A is non-zero, ORs bit 4 into the encoding byte at a2+25; then, when the bit depth byte at a2+24 is below 8, forces it to 8, and always zeroes the WORD at a2+22.
When bit 0x20 of the flags byte at this+0x61 is set, copies the DWORD at this+0x130 (camera rotation data) into the packet DWORD at a2+40.
When bit 0x4 of the flags byte at this+0x61 is set and the packet bit depth byte at a2+24 is 16, downgrades the bit depth to 8.
When bit 0x40 of the flags DWORD at this+0x60 is set, the encoding byte at a2+25 is 2 or 6, the DWORD at this+0x174 is non-zero, and the packet bit depth at a2+24 is 8, sets the encoding byte to 3.
When bit 0x4 of the flags DWORD at this+0x60 is set and the packet bit depth byte at a2+24 is below 8, raises the bit depth to 8.

Computes the per-sample stride byte at a2+29 from the encoding byte at a2+25: 1 when the encoding is 3 or lacks bit 2, else 3; increments the stride when bit 4 of the encoding is set; increments again when the sign bit of this+0x61 is set and the encoding is 2 or 0.
Multiplies the stride byte at a2+29 by the bit depth byte at a2+24, storing the total bytes-per-sample product in the byte at a2+30.
Computes result = (DWORD at a2 * bytes-per-sample product + 7) >> 3, stores it in the DWORD at a2+12, and returns it as the encoded packet field size.

unresolved: The output packet object at a2 is not part of the packet evidence; the exact layout and semantics of a2+0, a2+12, a2+22, a2+24, a2+25, a2+29, a2+30, and a2+40 are inferred from the raw source text only.
The encoded meaning of the encoding-type values (2, 3, 6) and bit-depth values (8, 16) is not grounded in packet evidence.
The owning class of this is unknown; a1 is only shown to carry flag bytes at 0x60/0x61 and configuration at 0x10A, 0x130, and 0x174.
Why bit 0x4 of this+0x60 and bit 0x4 of this+0x61 both modify the same bit-depth byte is unexplained.
